answer:
To run the Ollama container with access to all NVIDIA GPUs, first install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, then start the container with `--gpus=all`.

1. Install the toolkit. The docs link to NVIDIA's install guide: "Install the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit]" [ollama/docs/docker.md].

2. Configure Docker to use the NVIDIA runtime and restart it:
   ```shell
   sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
   sudo systemctl restart docker
   ```
   [ollama/docs/docker.md]

3. Start the container:
   ```shell
   docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
   ```
   The line in the docs is "docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama" [ollama/docs/docker.md].

If you want to limit Ollama to specific GPUs, the docs say to set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`: "you can set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to a comma separated list of GPUs" [ollama/docs/gpu.md].

To check that GPU passthrough works, the docs suggest: "Try `docker run --gpus all ubuntu nvidia-smi` - if this doesn't work, Ollama won't be able to see your NVIDIA GPU." [ollama/docs/troubleshooting.md]
